approach: Add `check_behavior_test_reading` to crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs, gated by the existing `changes_code_with_behavior_criterion`, and wire it as one `step!` line directly after `step!(check_code_survey(reading))` in checks.rs. The reader states four labelled assumptions (`Gate order:`, `Reuses:`, `Record kind:`, `Direct check:`), and each label is matched lexically on its own assumption line. The check collects every missing or contradicting part into one error that names the parts as "(a) gate order and stop gate", "(b) reused existing function", "(c) record kind or round-trip deliverable" and "(d) direct check", and also names the check itself, so the `refuse:` line of `athena check-reading` shows it. For (c) it reuses `names_record_evidence` and `is_record_or_data_deliverable`. For (b) it reuses `names_existing_path`. Existing fixtures are made complete by one test helper that appends the four clauses. New tests: a unit module in reading.rs, corpus cases in refusal_corpus.rs, a replay test over past-shaped readings (using `replay` from replay.rs), and a CLI case. The reader brief gets one added sentence in `CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE`, and the section-size bounds in briefs.rs rise by the measured growth. CHANGELOG.md gets an entry that states the limits of skip-switch matching. No prompt file, record, athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflow is touched.

decisions.choice: The four parts are four separate labelled assumptions: `Gate order:`, `Reuses:`, `Record kind:`, `Direct check:`. Each is matched by `starts_with` after trim, in any case. A small generic helper `assumptions_labeled(reading, label)` returns the bodies and sits beside `code_surveys` and `environment_assumptions`.
decisions.reason: This is the pattern of `Code survey:`, `Environment:` and `Existing code:` (surveys.rs:117-124, 605-612, 1329-1336). Separate labels let the error name exactly which part is missing, and AC2 needs that. They are 'new required labels that past readings never used', which is why AC4 declares 30%.

rejected.option: Look for the four parts as free prose inside the existing `Code survey:` assumption.
rejected.why: Prose cannot say which part is missing, and it would need a stem list that is hard to test. The existing survey already passes with a single sentence (reading.rs:7037).

rejected.option: Put the four clauses in the criteria text.
rejected.why: Criteria are judged by the verifier. `check_records_measure` shows the trouble: a criterion that mentions a measure triggers rules on itself.

decisions.choice: Part (a) needs a `Gate order:` body with at least two code identifiers (a token with `_` or `::`, not a path or a file name) and a stop-gate phrase (`stop gate`, `stops at`, `stops after` or `stop at`). Part (b) needs a `Reuses:` body with an identifier and a `crates/` path the job does not create (`names_existing_path` plus `names_crates_path`). Part (c) needs a `Record kind:` body that satisfies `names_record_evidence`, or the word `none`, or a round-trip test deliverable (a deliverable path whose file name holds `round_trip`, `roundtrip` or `round-trip`). `none` is accepted only when no deliverable satisfies `is_record_or_data_deliverable`. Part (d) needs each non-routine behavior criterion to be named as `criterion N` in a `Direct check:` body, and that body must hold a code identifier.
decisions.reason: This reuses the helpers the brief names (`names_record_evidence` at surveys.rs:164 and `is_record_or_data_deliverable` at surveys.rs:140). It makes the record contradiction of AC3 checkable from the deliverable list alone, with no repository read. Naming a criterion by number lets the error say which criterion lacks a direct check.

rejected.why: A new record file with 'none' is the contradiction AC3 requires the check to refuse.

rejected.option: Count `Direct check:` assumptions against the number of criteria.
rejected.why: It cannot say which property is unchecked, and it fails when one assumption covers two criteria.

decisions.choice: A skip switch or an internal-helper read in a `Direct check:` body is refused unless negated. Skip switches are tokens that contain `skip_`, `_skip` or `no_probe`, or start with `athena_no_` or `athena_skip_` (so `skip_probe` and `ATHENA_NO_PROBE` match). Internal-helper phrases are `internal helper`, `private helper`, `stand-in`, `through a helper` and `via a helper`. A mention is negated when `no`, `not`, `never`, `without`, `nor`, `than`, `instead` or `avoid` sits in the four tokens before it. The CHANGELOG states the limit: only these spellings are matched, and a switch under another name, or one described in prose, is not caught.
decisions.reason: AC3 names `skip_probe` and `ATHENA_NO_PROBE`, accepts a negated mention, and asks for the limit to be stated in CHANGELOG. The other lexical checks here (`check_history_fixture`, `check_records_measure`) state their limits the same way.

rejected.option: Refuse any mention of a skip switch.
rejected.why: A reading that says 'not through skip_probe' would be refused for stating the right property; AC3 says that is accepted.

rejected.option: Detect skip switches by reading the repository.
rejected.why: The reading checks read the `Reading` only, with no repository, records or network (surveys.rs:310-311).

decisions.choice: A criterion is routine, and needs no `Direct check:`, when it has the word pass, passes or passing, at least one of fmt, clippy or test(s), and every word is in a short stop list (`cargo`, `fmt`, `clippy`, `test`, `tests`, `check`, `pass`, `passes`, `passing`, `and`, `the`, `on`, `final`, `tree`, `still`, `all`, `locked`, `same`, `as`, a, `recorded`, `athena`). Parts (a)-(c) are still required for such a reading.
decisions.reason: AC3 says a routine criterion needs no direct-check clause. Such a criterion is not a property of the change.

rejected.option: Skip the whole check when every behavior criterion is routine.
rejected.why: AC2 requires parts (a)-(c) for every code or tests reading with a behavior criterion.

decisions.choice: `check_behavior_test_reading` is a new `pub fn` in surveys.rs. Its doc comment carries the root-cause sentence and the sentence 'This check refuses more readings; the higher refusal rate is intended', plus 'expected 30% of newly refused readings', 'estimate' and 'Limits:'. The error text ends by naming `check_behavior_test_reading` and gives an example of the four clauses.
decisions.reason: `check_reading_text` returns only the error text and drops the check name (checks.rs:492-503, replay.rs:54-65). AC5 needs the `refuse:` line to name the check, so the name goes in the message. The doc-comment sentences are what the existing `*_refusal_is_declared_intended` corpus tests read (refusal_corpus.rs:3090-3207).

rejected.option: Change `check_reading_text` to return the check name.
rejected.why: That changes `ReadingCheck`, `BinaryChecker::parse` and the `refuse:` line format that the replay parses (replay.rs:35-47), which is more than the goal needs.

decisions.choice: Extend the reader brief by one sentence in `CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE` (reader.rs:356) and raise `READING_RULES_BASELINE_BYTES` (briefs.rs:3591) and the `3150` cap (briefs.rs:3710) by the measured growth. Add no rule line, so `READING_RULES.len()` stays 12.
decisions.reason: Without the labels in the brief, the reader would meet the refusal only on the second and last read. The reading-rules section is measured as brief text, outside the prompt budget sets (briefs.rs:3704-3710 comment). No prompt file is edited, so the reader budget of 1998 of 2000 does not move. Adding a rule line would break `assert_eq!(READING_RULES.len(), 12)` (briefs.rs:3653) and the 220-byte line cap.

rejected.why: It breaks the count assertion at briefs.rs:3653 and grows the section more than one sentence in the guide does.

rejected.option: Edit the reader prompt under crates/athena-context/prompts/.
rejected.why: The brief puts prompt files out of scope, and the reader budget is 1998 of 2000.

decisions.choice: The replay test goes in the existing replay test group of reading.rs (next to `replay_hold_is_over_ten_percent_without_a_declared_share`, reading.rs:6625). It calls `replay` from replay.rs with real `check_reading_text` as the candidate. The base is a closure that runs the same real gate on the reading with the four clauses added. The test uses a window of past-shaped readings (docs, content-only and feature readings, and code readings with one-line surveys) and declares 30%. It asserts the newly refused job ids and `replay_is_held(total, newly, Some(30))` is false. replay.rs gets no code change.
decisions.reason: The replay machinery and its tests already live there (reading.rs:6459-7010). A reading helper such as `scoped_reading` is private to that test module. `records/` is absent from a producer snapshot, so the real share can be measured only by the replay Athena runs at verification; the test covers the mechanics and the declared bound on fixtures.

rejected.option: Read recent accepted readings from `records/` inside a test.
rejected.why: records/ and history are absent from the producer snapshot (system facts, 'Producer snapshot'), so the test would skip or fail.

rejected.option: Add a test module to replay.rs.
rejected.why: It would need its own Reading builder, and the child-module text is concatenated into `reading_source()` for the source-reading tests (reading.rs:1578-1593).

decisions.choice: status.rs and verify.rs are not changed even though they are listed as deliverables.
decisions.reason: Neither reads the list of check names. status.rs groups refusals by the recorded rule string (status.rs:226) and only names `check_code_survey` as a test constant (status.rs:3908). verify.rs reads the generic replay hold (verify.rs:500-526). A change there would be a change with no purpose.

rejected.why: It would be an unrelated behavior change, which AC8 forbids.

risks.risk: The real newly-refused share on the newest 50 accepted readings may exceed 35%. Most past code readings used a one-line survey, so every code or tests reading with a behavior criterion is newly refused. The in-repo replay test uses fixtures and cannot measure the real share.
risks.mitigation: AC4 forbids loosening. The plan reports the measured share and the newly refused job ids if the replay is above 35%. The 30% is declared with the reason sentence, as the replay rules require above 25%. The in-repo replay test covers the mechanics only.

risks.risk: The reader may fail the second and last read if the labels are unfamiliar.
risks.mitigation: The error names the missing parts and gives one example clause for each. `CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE` names the labels so the first read already includes them. Labels are matched after trim and in any case.

risks.risk: Lexical matching of skip switches and internal-helper phrases misses other names, and the negation window can accept a mention that is not really negated.
risks.mitigation: The changelog and doc comment state the limit. Matching covers only the listed spellings, and a negation window of four tokens. Corpus cases pin the accepted and refused forms.

risks.risk: Many existing reading.rs and corpus fixtures use the short survey and would be newly refused, and a missed site fails the test suite.
risks.mitigation: The helper change is in one place (`code_reading` and the corpus survey constant). The producer lists every call site found in this plan and runs `cargo test -p athena-core` and `-p athena-cli`.

risks.risk: The reader brief section is capped at 3045 bytes by an existing test. Adding the sentence could break it if the bound is not raised by the right amount.
risks.mitigation: The producer measures the guide growth and sets the new bounds to that value, not a larger one. The reader prompt files are not edited, so the 1998 of 2000 budget does not move.

demonstrations.method: The test `behavior_test_replay_stays_within_the_declared_share` is added in reading.rs next to the existing replay tests. Entry point: `replay(&cases, &base, &candidate, declared)` from replay.rs, with `declared = replay_declaration_of(&reading).effective_share()` read from a Reading whose criterion 4 is the AC4 text, so the 30% and the reason sentence are parsed by the real code. The candidate is the real gate (`check_reading_text`). The base is a closure that runs the same real gate on the reading with the four clauses appended; the test first asserts every fixture is accepted by that base. The fixtures are ten past-shaped readings: docs, feature and content-only readings, and code readings with a one-line `Code survey:` and a behavior criterion. The test asserts that the newly refused ids are exactly the code behavior readings, that `replay_is_held(total, newly, Some(30))` is false, and that with no declared share the same run is held. No marker is loosened. The real share over the newest 50 accepted readings in `records/` is measured by Athena's own replay at verification and recorded in `replay.json`; if it is above 35%, the plan reports the share and the newly refused job ids and does not loosen any marker.
demonstrations.observes: The replay lists exactly the code behavior readings as newly refused. It is held without a declared share and not held with 30 declared.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the new check the candidate equals the base, so the newly refused list is empty and the id assertion fails. If the check also refused docs or content-only readings, the id assertion would fail.
demonstrations.seam: `replay` and `replay_declaration_of` (exist, replay.rs:263-290, 365); the candidate is the production gate `check_reading_text`; the base closure uses the same production gate on a reading with clauses added, so the logic under test is not inside the double; the test is added by the plan.

demonstrations.method: Production entry point: `check_reading_command(request, reading)` in crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs:687, which calls `check_reading_text`. The seam is the test fixture function `reading_json` (main.rs:1211), which writes the reading file in a tempdir (exists). The plan step generalizes it to `reading_json_for(criterion, class, assumptions)`, with `reading_json` calling it with class `feature` and no assumptions. The existing test `check_reading_prints_accept_for_a_reading_the_rules_accept` (main.rs:1277) keeps the class 'feature' fixture and must still print `accept`. A new test `check_reading_refuses_a_code_reading_with_a_short_survey` uses class `code`, the assumption 'Code survey: crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs was read', and the criterion 'Run `cargo test -p athena-core`: the greeting is printed'. It asserts exit code 2, a line that starts `refuse: `, holds `check_behavior_test_reading` and `(a) gate order and stop gate`, and has no newline. A second assertion shows that the same reading with the four clauses prints `accept`.
demonstrations.observes: The class 'feature' reading prints `accept`. The code reading with a short survey prints a `refuse:` line naming the new check.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the check the code reading with a short survey would print `accept` with exit code 0, so the exit code and `refuse:` assertions fail.
demonstrations.seam: `check_reading_command` (exists, main.rs:687); the reading file is a tempdir fixture (exists); the generalized `reading_json_for` and the new test are added by the plan.
